subject: Request: 'No-Access' attestation & local key custody for private deployment
messages:
From: Alyssa Greene <dpo@bluecresthealth.com>

Cc: legal@bluecresthealth.com

Subject: Request: 'No-Access' attestation & local key custody for private deployment

Marissa / Logan,

Thanks for the private deployment overview last week. BlueCrest is moving forward with a VPC-onprem pilot and procurement is seeking a few clarifications before we finalize the DPA addendum. Two specific asks from legal & security: 

1) A written attestation that Redwood personnel will have no access to customer plaintext data ("no-access attestation") when the deployment is configured with customer-controlled keys and with the control plane isolated. We need the exact scope of that attestation (what "access" covers, whether it includes metadata/telemetry, and the limits of breakglass) so the legal team can sign-off.

2) A description of the key custody model for the on-premises/VPC deployment: who generates keys, where CMKs/HSMs are held, the rotation/escrow policy, and how operator breakglass is audited. If you have a standard template attestation and an architecture diagram that highlights control-plane vs data-plane responsibilities, please attach.

We attached the DPA addendum template with our proposed markings. Can you respond with the attestation draft and a short runbook for breakglass in case of incident? Procurement needs this by end of week to keep the timeline.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a call if it's easier.

Best,
Alyssa Greene
Data Protection Officer
BlueCrest Health

Attachments: DPA_Addendum_Template_v2.pdf

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: 'No-Access' attestation & local key custody for private deployment

Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear asks and for sending the addendum. We can provide both: a concise "no-access" attestation letter and a technical appendix that covers key generation, custody, and the breakglass audit trail. High-level answers here to set expectations: 

- No-access attestation: Redwood will confirm that with customer-managed CMKs and the recommended control-plane isolation configuration, Redwood engineers will not have routine access to customer plaintext content. We will clarify that limited metadata (service telemetry required for operations) is still collected unless you opt into reduced telemetry — we can mark what that includes.

- Key custody: We support BYOK/HSM-based key custody. Keys can be generated by the customer or provisioned into an HSM under customer control. Our standard on-prem connector supports an external KMS. Escrow/rotation is contractually optional — we will provide an escrow workflow if you need it; otherwise, keys remain solely under customer custody.

Next steps: I'll draft the attestation and a one-page breakglass runbook, and attach an architecture diagram that highlights data-plane encryption boundaries. Logan, can you add the technical note about operator roles and minimum-privilege controls? Evelyn, please include a short paragraph we can add to the DPA addendum about subprocessor notification timing.

We should be able to get you a packet by close of business Thu (07/16). If procurement needs faster turnaround, let us know.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments to follow: attestation-draft.docx, breakglass-runbook.pdf

Subject: Re: Request: 'No-Access' attestation & local key custody for private deployment

Alyssa / Marissa —

Quick technical clarifications to add context for the attestation draft: 

- Separation of concerns: In the recommended deployment, the data-plane processes (model inference, tokenization, KV cache) run inside the customer's VPC/on-prem network and are encrypted at-rest and in-transit with the customer CMK. The control plane (scheduling, model registry pointers, monitoring hooks) can be run in Redwood's managed plane or in a customer-hosted control plane per the Private offering. Our attestation will reference the option you choose; the "no-access" statement is strongest when the control plane is customer-hosted or when we operate only a thin control plane without access to KV caches or ciphertext keys.

- Breakglass: Our breakglass flow is role-based and requires a documented incident declaration, multi-party approval (security + customer ops), and a time-limited KEK unwrap. Every breakglass event generates an immutable audit record (timestamp, approvers, operator identities, and a signed justification). We also produce a signed evidence bundle (logs + KMS unwrap events) for customer retention.

- Subprocessors: Redwood's managed control plane uses a small set of third-party infra providers. For Private with customer-controlled keys and fully isolated control-plane, operator access to plaintext is technically prevented; however, we will commit to pre-notification and approval of any subprocessor that would materially change that assumption.

See the linked diagram for the boundary calls: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleArcDiagram

I will attach a short technical appendix (1 page) that describes the HSM/KMS handshake, key rotation windows, and the log artifact structure.

—Logan
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: technical-appendix-keyflow.pdf

This is helpful. A few remaining items before procurement can finalize: 

- Please include explicit language in the attestation excluding routine access "for development or debugging" but describing the breakglass exception process and the evidence we will receive.
- We need a signed SAP (Service Access Policy) appendix committing to 30-days notice for any new subprocessor that would have the ability to affect key custody or control-plane components.
- Please provide a current list of subprocessors and SOC 2/AICPA references or a recent summary of controls; attached is our vendor subproc list for your reference.

If you can return the attestation and the SAP appendix by EOD Monday (07/20), procurement can complete the PO. If any of these require legal redlines, please mark them directly in the DPA addendum and flag the change log.

Regards,
BlueCrest Health Legal
